paper_design_summary: A descriptive formative study had 16 engineers write an unassisted Japanese short story for 40 minutes and reused their 152 self-reported writing-block events for cognitive-process prediction (pp. 5-6, Secs. 3.2-3.3; p. 8, Sec. 3.6). Two counterbalanced within-person experiments then evaluated AToM CoWriter (Claude Sonnet 4) with 11 and 10 engineers: the 21 participants were randomly allocated between studies, condition-order randomization was not stated, and 14 had also participated in the formative study (pp. 10-11, Secs. 4.2-5.1). The user evaluations measured self-reported creativity support, workload and related perceptions, plus suggestion engagement in Study 2; they reported no creativity or diversity scoring of the stories (pp. 11-13, Secs. 5.1-5.3).

studies.label: Study 1 (System-Inferred vs. User-Articulated support, short story writing)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Each participant used both conditions (System-Inferred proactive + prompt-less support vs. User-Articulated prompt-based chat only), one per story; order counterbalanced via Latin square. Random assignment is stated only for allocation of participants to Study 1 or Study 2, not for condition order.
assignment.quote: Twenty-one participants (engineers at a technology company, all frequent LLM users; IRB approved) were randomly assigned to Study 1 or Study 2. ... with conditions counterbalanced via Latin square.

arms.name: System-Inferred
arms.description: Proactive (inactivity-triggered, 20 s) and prompt-less (Help button) support in which the system infers what support to give; free chat also available

arms.name: User-Articulated
arms.description: Prompt-based chat interface only; users formulate explicit requests

participants.who: Engineers at a technology company (appendix C.1: a manufacturing company), all frequent LLM users; 14 of the 21 user-study participants had also taken part in the formative study
participants.quote: Study 1 (n = 11) examined the impact of system-inferred proactive support compared to user-articulated prompt-based support.

ai_tool.name_model: AToM CoWriter, multi-agent system powered by Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4 (claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0)
ai_tool.how_used: A Main Agent activates up to three Functional Agents (14 support types) that produce panel outputs and inline suggestions when the writer is idle or presses a Help button (treatment); the comparison condition offers only the prompt-based chat (p. 10, Sec. 4.2; p. 11, Sec. 5.1)

task.description: Short story on an assigned theme (around 400 characters per custom instruction, p. 24, C.8); two stories per participant, one per condition
task.duration: 20-25 minutes per story; about 90 minutes per session

contrasts.reported: Expressiveness (CSI): p 0.005 (Holm 0.034), RBC 0.924, CLES 0.669; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, n = 11; arm scores shown only as box plots (Fig. 7)
Total Score (CSI): p 0.083 (Holm 0.498), RBC 0.606, CLES 0.678; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test

studies.label: Study 2 (w/ Cog vs. w/o Cog proactive support, short story writing)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Each participant used both proactive conditions (w/ Cog: cognitive-process inference from interaction logs plus document text; w/o Cog: document text only), one per story; order counterbalanced via Latin square. Random assignment is stated only for allocation to Study 1 or Study 2.
assignment.quote: Twenty-one participants (engineers at a technology company, all frequent LLM users; IRB approved) were randomly assigned to Study 1 or Study 2. ... with conditions counterbalanced via Latin square.

arms.name: w/ Cog
arms.description: Proactive + prompt-less + chat; support selection uses real-time cognitive-process inference from interaction logs and document content

arms.name: w/o Cog
arms.description: Proactive + prompt-less + chat; support selection uses only the evolving document content

participants.who: Engineers at a technology company (appendix C.1: a manufacturing company), all frequent LLM users
participants.quote: Study 2 (n = 10) isolated the effect of incorporating cognitive process inference from interaction logs within the proactive paradigm.

ai_tool.name_model: AToM CoWriter, multi-agent system powered by Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4 (claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0)
ai_tool.how_used: Proactive and button-triggered Functional Agent outputs (panel content and inline suggestions) plus chat in both arms; arms differ only in whether interaction-log features feed the support selection (p. 11, Sec. 5.1)

task.description: Short story on an assigned theme; two stories per participant, one per condition
task.duration: 20-25 minutes per story; about 90 minutes per session

outcomes.name: Suggestion conversion/engagement
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Interaction-log engagement with inline Suggest Output: whether participants opened a suggestion (p. 12, Sec. 5.3). Figure 9 plots average conversion counts per session with SE error bars and individual participant counts (p. 13); Sec. 5.3 separately reports descriptive suggestion open rates. The paper does not explicitly identify whether the Wilcoxon test uses counts or proportions.

contrasts.reported: Suggestion conversion: one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank W = 26, p = 0.031 (Holm p_adj = 0.094), r = 0.86; not significant after Holm correction. Separately reported descriptive suggestion open rates: 20.5% w/ Cog vs. 7.4% w/o Cog. Figure 9 shows conversion counts; the paper does not explicitly identify the Wilcoxon statistic as a test of these open-rate proportions. Tabs and Panel conversion: no significant differences (Tabs r = 0.51).

studies.label: Formative study (unassisted Japanese story writing and cognitive-process prediction)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Descriptive single-condition study: all participants wrote without AI assistance and chose their own story theme; repeated self-reports were collected within participants. No AI-assistance or condition-order contrast was assigned (p. 5, Sec. 3.2; p. 11, Sec. 5.1).
assignment.quote: The formative study used a self-report annotation tool (Fig. 2) with no AI assistance,

arms.name: Unassisted writing with data logging
arms.description: Data-logging editor with self-report annotation; no AI writing assistance or external tools (p. 5, Sec. 3.2; p. 11, Sec. 5.1).

participants.who: Engineers from a manufacturing company, all regular LLM users, recruited through internal Slack channels (p. 5, Sec. 3.2).
participants.quote: Sixteen engineers from a manufacturing company participated in the study

ai_tool.name_model: No AI writing assistance; Claude 3.5 Sonnet used in later cognitive-process prediction analysis
ai_tool.how_used: Participants used only the data-logging/self-report editor while writing. Offline cognitive-process prediction compared Claude 3.5 Sonnet using logs plus document text or document text alone, and LightGBM using logs alone; this evaluation reused the same 152 annotated events and did not assign AI writing assistance to people (p. 8, Sec. 3.6; p. 11, Sec. 5.1; p. 19, Appx. A.3).

task.description: Write a short story on a self-chosen theme in Japanese, using only the provided editor, with ideas and outlines entered in the same editor (p. 5, Sec. 3.2).

outcomes.name: Cognitive-process self-reports at writing blocks
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Each observation is a self-report annotation of the current cognitive process, difficulty, and desired support at a writing block; unit rating refers to an annotation, not a distinct person. There were 152 events from 16 people, and the cognitive-process prediction evaluation reused these events. These annotations and classification results do not score story creativity or diversity (pp. 4-6, Secs. 3.1.1-3.3; p. 8, Sec. 3.6; p. 19, Appx. A.3).

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Within this paper, 14 of the 21 user-evaluation participants (S1 and S2 combined) also participated in the formative study F1. The distribution of these 14 across S1 and S2 is not reported. The cognitive-process prediction analysis reuses F1's 152 self-report events, not a new participant sample.
sample_overlap.quote: Fourteen participants had also participated in the formative study;

company_involvement.description: Masahiro Yoshida, Atsuya Kobayashi, and Kei Tateno list Sony Group Corporation as their affiliation.

eligibility.reason: The formative study is descriptive and unassisted (16 people), and the two user studies analyze 11 and 10 people; every study is below 50 participants (p. 5, Sec. 3.2; p. 11, Sec. 5.1). Both conditions in each user study use generative AI and are counterbalanced via Latin square; random assignment is reported only for allocation between studies, so randomization of condition order remains unclear (p. 11, Sec. 5.1). The formative study's 152 self-report events are observations, not people, and 14 user-evaluation participants overlap with that sample (p. 8, Sec. 3.6; p. 11, Sec. 5.1). No study reports an eligible comparison of creativity or diversity scored on human outputs: formative outcomes concern cognitive processes and support needs, the prediction evaluation classifies those processes, and the user evaluations use questionnaires and interaction logs (pp. 6, 8, 11-13, 19, 22). These studies belong only in the screening report, with no core or context evidence.

one_line_finding: In Study 1 (n = 11), self-reported CSI Expressiveness was higher with system-inferred support (Holm p = 0.034, RBC = 0.924; p. 22, Table 7); Study 2 (n = 10) reported descriptive suggestion open rates of 20.5% w/ Cog versus 7.4% w/o Cog, while the Suggestion conversion test was not significant after Holm correction (W = 26, p = 0.031, Holm p = 0.094; pp. 12-13, Sec. 5.3; sample sizes: p. 11, Sec. 5.1).
